claims.text: Ultra-rapid melt spinning followed by controlled sub-Tg annealing will improve both glass-forming ability and amorphous-state thermal stability relative to ultra-rapid melt spinning alone.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 is an example of a phosphorus-containing compositionally complex alloy capable of amorphization by melt spinning.
Melt-spun Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 exhibits only partial amorphization.
The initially melt-spun alloy has limited resistance to crystallization during heating.
Rapid cooling during melt spinning can suppress crystallization and produce an amorphous Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 ribbon.
Typical rapid-solidification cooling rates for the proposed intervention are approximately 10^5–10^6 K/s.
Annealing below Tg for a short duration will promote structural relaxation without inducing crystallization.
Phosphorus significantly enhances the amorphization tendency of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Compositions that deviate substantially from the relevant high-entropy design may not benefit from the proposed annealing treatment.
High-entropy effects can induce glass-to-glass transitions that yield low-energy glasses with excellent thermal stability.
The proposed sub-Tg anneal will cause either structural relaxation or a beneficial glass-to-glass transition in the phosphorus-containing alloy.
The annealing-induced state will be denser and more homogeneous and will contain less free volume.
Reduced free volume in the relaxed amorphous matrix will inhibit crystalline-phase nucleation and growth.
Sub-Tg annealing will facilitate atomic rearrangement, relax internal stresses, and optimize the short-range order formed during quenching.
The proposed relaxation will lower the driving force for crystallization during subsequent heating.
The proposed relaxation will increase the kinetic barrier to subsequent crystallization.
The combined treatment will produce a higher amorphous fraction than melt spinning alone.
The combined treatment will raise or delay the DSC crystallization-onset temperature relative to melt spinning alone.
The benefit will diminish if the annealing temperature is not optimally maintained below Tg.
